sourceDocs: BMS Training Manual 4.38.1 - Mission 12 (AGM-88 HARMs), Mission 28 (SEAD-EW)
BMS User Manual 4.38.1 - 5.1.7 DTC HARM tab
BMS Threat Guide (Air Defense Vehicle charts)
overview: In BMS the AGM-88 HARM can be employed in three modes. POS (Position Known) fires the missile at a steerpoint (usually a PPT or markpoint) rather than at a radar: after launch it flies toward the steerpoint and opens its seeker at a trip point that depends on the submode - EOM (Equations Of Motion, narrow FOV, ~8 NM from the threat, most accurate), PB (Pre-Briefed, ~13 NM, wider FOV, long-range shots) or RUK (Range Unknown, ~30 NM, wide FOV, mainly self-defence). HAS (HARM As Sensor) uses the missile seeker itself (120 deg FOV) to display up to 10 emitting radars from the selected threat table on the WPN page; a detected threat is handed off with TMS up and the page is lost once the last HARM is fired. HAD (HARM Attack Display) is only available with the AN/ASQ-213 HTS pod (US F-16 Block 40/50/52 in BMS, left chin pylon): the pod passively detects and triangulates all radars (not limited to threat tables), shows them on an HSD-like page with PGM5 (worst) to PGM1 (best) position quality, and hands the estimated position to the missile which is then actually fired in POS mode (EOM or RUK chosen automatically from the PGM index, TMS up long to override). The DL mode is not implemented. Threats are loaded through three threat tables (TBL1-TBL3), each holding five entries (max 15 radars). Each entry is an ALIC code (decimal ID 0-4095, must be unique across all tables) for either a complete SAM system (e.g. 102 = SA-2, symbol "2"), its fire control/tracking radar ("T" suffix, e.g. 202 = Fan Song "2T") or its acquisition/early-warning radar ("A" suffix, e.g. 402 = Spoon Rest "2A"). If a SAM system code is loaded, both its FCR and EWR are searched. Tables are set in the DTC HARM tab (all codes default to 0000 - no defaults), or in the cockpit via ICP 0 (HARM DED page, A-G mode with HARM selected) or OSB 5 "UFC" on the POS/HAS page. The TER (tertiary) table is selected on the SMS page with OSB 2 (TBL0-TBL3, default TBL1; TBL0 = no tertiary targets): primary target = the handed-off threat, secondary = remaining threats of the active table (or HAD priority targets), tertiary = threats of the TER table. Target Isolate (TI: FLEX / GLIDE, OSB 10 or UNCAGE) and Geographic Specificity (GS, OSB 9) refine what the seeker will accept after launch.

modes.name: POS - Equations Of Motion (EOM)
modes.description: Most restrictive/accurate POS submode. The seeker activates with a narrow FOV at approx. 8 NM from the anticipated threat position (the handed-off steerpoint). Use only when the emitter location is well known, i.e. collocated with a steerpoint/PPT (fixed sites, or mobile SAMs that have stopped and been marked). HUD HARM FOV box is smallest in EOM; TOF/TOT (pre-launch) and TUI (post-launch) timers are shown on the WPN page, allowing pre-emptive (PET) shots timed to a package trespass.

hotas.effect: Cycles POS submodes EOM / PB / RUK (OSB 3 hands-off)
POS/HAD: cycles HARM submodes
POS: cycles threats of the selected threat table (hands off the threat type)
Toggles between threat tables (OSB 2 hands-off)
Toggles between POS and HAS (WPN page SOI)
Steps to the next HARM station (each station remembers its own threat, submode and mode)
Toggles Target Isolate option (OSB 10 hands-off)
Launch - hold until the missile is away

steps: A-G master mode, MASTER ARM - ARM, SMS page OSB 7 PWR ON (all HARMs of that type power up; ~10 s BIT, RDY when complete). AA FCR (CRM) recommended for SA - the A-G FCR is not needed.

Select the target steerpoint/PPT as current steerpoint (ICP STPT, or HSD SOI: cursor over the PPT and TMS up). All HARMs are handed off with the CURRENT steerpoint - change steerpoint before each shot at a different location.
WPN page: select POS with OSB 1 or Cursor Enable, choose EOM with OSB 3 / pinky.
Select the threat table (OSB 2 / TMS left) and hand off a threat type with OSB 16-20 or TMS right. Best practice: select the SAM system (e.g. "2") rather than a single radar.
Set TI (OSB 10) and GS (OSB 9) options as briefed - each change restarts the handoff.
Wait for handoff: threat highlighted and RDY at the bottom of the HUD (SIM in Master Arm SIM). A missile launched before handoff completes will fail.
Steer with the Azimuth Steering Line; fire when the HARM FOV box flashes and the range caret is between Rmin and Rmax on the HARM Launch Scale (or at the planned TOT for SEAD suppression).
Radio the launch (e.g. "Weasel 3-1, Magnum PET Alpha 2 minutes") and call the timeout when TUI reaches 0:00 ("Weasel 3-1, PET Alpha timeout"). Be ready to trim for the asymmetric load.
modes.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 4.2.5.1.4.1, 4.2.5.1.5; BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 12

modes.name: POS - Pre-Briefed (PB)
modes.description: Long-range delivery with high confidence in the target location. The seeker activates at approx. 13 NM from the steerpoint with a wider FOV than EOM. WPN page identical to EOM; the HUD shows the larger HARM FOV and an optimal loft cue between > < carets on the ASL. If the relative bearing exceeds 5 deg in PB, TOF is computed assuming zero relative bearing.

hotas.effect: Selects PB in the EOM / PB / RUK cycle
Cycles/hands off threats from the selected table
Toggles threat tables

steps: Same set-up as POS EOM (power, steerpoint, table, threat handoff, TI/GS).
Select PB with OSB 3 or the pinky switch.
Use the optimal loft cue and in-range cues in the HUD; launch at long range when confident in the target position.
modes.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 4.2.5.1.4.1, 4.2.5.1.9; BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 12

modes.name: POS - Range Unknown (RUK)
modes.description: Degraded EOM mode with high uncertainty about threat range, used mainly defensively. The seeker activates approx. 30 NM from the steerpoint (in most cases at launch) with a wide FOV. TOF, TOT and TUI are not displayed; the HLS ranges (Rmax/Rmin) and loft cues are not available. Be careful with TI = FLEX: the missile may take an emitter well short of the target.

hotas.effect: Selects RUK in the EOM / PB / RUK cycle
Cycles/hands off threats from the selected table

steps: Same set-up as POS EOM, then select RUK with OSB 3 or pinky.
Point the missile at the threat area (wide HUD HARM FOV) and launch; no timers or range cues are provided.
modes.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 4.2.5.1.4.1; BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 12

modes.name: HAS - HARM As Sensor
modes.description: The HARM seeker is the sensor: the WPN page shows the ALIC (Aircraft Launcher Interface Computer) display - the missile WIDE field of view (120 deg) - with up to 10 emitting radars that belong to the selected threat table, positioned by elevation/azimuth (roll and pitch stabilized). Threat position does not need to be known, but the radar must be emitting. The Detected Threat Status Box (DTSB) lists detected threats; the scan cycle timer/counter show the search cycle (OSB 7 RS resets). If two radars of the same SAM system are close together they merge into the system symbol (e.g. 5A + 5T shown as "5"). No HUD in-range cues - range must be judged from the HSD/PPT rings (HARM range ~60-65 NM in BMS). The HAS page is unavailable once the last HARM has been fired.

hotas.effect: Toggles POS <-> HAS
Move the captain bars over a threat
Hands off the threat under the cursor (display changes to missile boresight view, only handed-off threat shown)
Selects the first valid threat; further presses step to the next threat / between radars of a handed-off SAM system
Deselects the threat and returns to normal scan cycle
Toggles threat tables (resets scan cycle timer)
Cycles FOV: WIDE / CENTER (front only, half range) / LT / RT - display resets on each change

steps: Pre-load threat tables (DTC or DED). WPN page OSB 1 -> HAS (OSB 19), or Cursor Enable from POS.
Optionally narrow the search: OSB 4 SRCH page, deselect threat types (OSB 16-20) per table (OSB 2) so no more than 10 emitters compete for the display; OSB 4/OSB 1 back to HAS.
Fly to make the SAM radiate (wild weasel / bait), staying outside its ring where possible.
WPN page SOI, slew cursor over the threat and TMS up (or TMS right). Handoff takes about 5 s and restarts if another radar is selected.
Wait for RDY above OSB 13 - missiles fired before handoff complete will miss.
Launch; keep baiting so the radar keeps emitting. Contacts that leave the HARM FOV blink and the page returns to HAS after 10 s.
modes.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 4.2.5.1.6, 4.2.5.1.7; BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 12

modes.name: HAD - HARM Attack Display (HTS pod)
modes.description: Requires the AN/ASQ-213 HTS pod (left chin station, LEFT HDPT power on the SNSR panel, otherwise "HTS OFF"). Selected from the MFD menu with OSB 2; usable in any master mode for detection, A-G mode to fire. HSD-like page (flight plan, PPTs and threat rings, datalink tracks, bullseye, range rings; range with OSB 19/20 or cursor bump; NORM/EXP1/EXP2 with OSB 3/pinky). Forward-looking only. Detects all radars (not limited to threat tables) and triangulates them: cursor readout shows bearing, major axis and minor axis of the error ellipse (NM, or ft below 1000 ft) and the PGM index (PGM5 = low confidence, PGM1 = high confidence). Emitter colors: green = detected but not currently radiating / outside pod FOV / behind 3-9 line, yellow = emitting; separate cues for priority target, primary target selected (white box) and handed off (filled pale magenta). The HTS gives no searching/tracking/guiding status. The missile is fired in POS mode at the estimated position (EOM or RUK auto-selected from PGM, TMS up long override; GS and TI behave as in POS). The HARM WEZ footprint (Rmax, depends on speed/altitude) is drawn dashed when larger than the displayed range. Lock is still possible after all HARMs are gone (to direct AI wingmen); since 4.36 a HAD lock can be used as SPI for FCR/TGP.

hotas.effect: Designates the contact as primary target and starts automatic handoff; a new TMS up makes the previous primary a priority target (up to 3)
Overrides the automatically selected HARM submode (EOM/RUK/PB)
Steps through priority targets (including the primary)
On a priority target: removes it from the list; in empty space: resets all priority targets and the primary
Cycles NORM / EXP1 / EXP2 FOV
Slew cursor; bump display range at the edges

steps: Load HTS + HARMs, LEFT HDPT power ON, A-G master mode, MASTER ARM ARM, SMS OSB 7 PWR ON.
Select HAD (MFD menu OSB 2), keep FCR in an A-A mode for SA.
Watch the RWR for the search radar (e.g. "L" Long Track) and the HAD for the emitter ("4A").
Beam the emitter (fly a bearing change) to triangulate - PGM improves from PGM5 toward PGM1 and the major/minor axes shrink. Flying straight at the radar does not help and is dangerous.
Target the fire control radar ("4T") when it comes up; EXP1 helps to select the right contact.
TMS up to lock/hand off (white box -> filled when handed off); TOF/impact time appear bottom right as in POS EOM.
Fire when the HUD HARM FOV/ASEC flashes in range; hold pickle until the missile leaves. Firing before handoff completes gives a dead missile.
Monitor time to impact; a destroyed radar turns green or disappears. Confirm with the TGP if possible.
modes.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 4.2.5.1.8; BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 12 (12.2)

optionsAndSettings.name: Threat tables TBL1-TBL3
optionsAndSettings.description: 5 entries each, decimal IDs 0-4095, IDs must be unique within and across tables. Cycle tables on the DED with the increment/decrement switch, move asterisks with the DCS, type the ID and ENTR. Access: ICP 0 (MISC page, HARM label, A-G mode with HARM selected) or OSB 5 UFC from POS/HAS.

optionsAndSettings.name: TER table (SMS OSB 2)
optionsAndSettings.description: Steps tertiary threat table TBL0-TBL3 (default TBL1). Tertiary targets of the selected table are loaded at handoff; TBL0 = no tertiary targets. Command Destruct (OSB 20) and Burst Height (OSB 19) are not implemented.

optionsAndSettings.name: SMS PWR / BIT
optionsAndSettings.description: OSB 7 PWR ON powers all HARMs of the selected type and starts a ~10 s BIT (RDY when successful). OSB 8 starts a manual BIT (can clear a faulty missile). No power time limit in BMS. Missiles stay powered until PWR OFF or an inventory change.
optionsAndSettings.source: TO 1F-16CMAM-34-1-1 BMS 4.2.5.1.2; BMS Training Manual 4.38.1, Mission 12

optionsAndSettings.name: Geographic Specificity (GS, OSB 9)
optionsAndSettings.description: Restricts the seeker to a circle around the selected steerpoint (POS) or target (HAS/HAD). Overrides all other seeker options. The restricted diameter grows with launch distance. GS-DE and GS-MP behave the same in BMS. Selecting GS restarts the handoff.

optionsAndSettings.name: Target Isolate (TI, OSB 10 or Uncage)
optionsAndSettings.description: FLEX: when the missile reaches the range at which it should have acquired the primary threat and has not, it searches for alternate threat emitter types (secondary/tertiary). GLIDE: maximizes time aloft to increase the chance of finding a threat. Neither: missile self-destructs/impacts at the target area.

optionsAndSettings.name: LOTG - Loss Of Track Glide
optionsAndSettings.description: Missile enters a gliding profile with the seeker opened wide when the primary threat was detected but then lost in flight (radar shut down), waiting for it (or another threat if FLEX) to come back.

optionsAndSettings.name: EOMG - Equation Of Motion Glide
optionsAndSettings.description: Missile enters a gliding profile with a wide seeker when the primary threat has not been detected after a certain point; also searches a footprint further from the handed-off steerpoint.

optionsAndSettings.name: Handoff
optionsAndSettings.description: All prelaunch parameters (mode, submode, table, primary threat, steerpoint, TI, GS) must be loaded into the missile; any change restarts the handoff. RDY in the HUD (or above OSB 13 in HAS) when complete. Unhanded-off launches fail/miss.

optionsAndSettings.name: HUD cues
optionsAndSettings.description: HARM FOV box (flashes when in range; smaller in EOM than PB/RUK), Azimuth Steering Line (like CCRP, shown in POS regardless of handoff), two loft solution cues on the ASL (plus optimal loft cue with carets in PB), HARM Launch Scale on the right (Rmax1/2, Rmin1/2, two 10 mR tics, in-range cue; ranges not available in RUK). Loft angle and apex altitude are not implemented.

optionsAndSettings.name: DTC HARM tab
optionsAndSettings.description: Defines the ALIC codes for TBL1-TBL3, initial delivery mode (HAS/POS), initial POS submode (PB/EOM/RUK) and initial TER table (TBL1/2/3/0). Codes default to 0000 (no defaults); fields take 4 digits but the 3-digit code can be entered without leading 0. Saved in pilot.ini when the DTC is saved.

defaultTables.name: No defaults in the DTC
defaultTables.description: The BMS DTC HARM tab has no default threat tables: on first start all ALIC codes in all tables are 0000. Tables must be set per mission according to the expected threats.

defaultTables.name: Example - Training Mission 12 (SA-2 / SA-4, KTO)
defaultTables.description: TBL1 as set in the DTC for TR_BMS_12_Harm: SA-2 system, Fan Song, Spoon Rest, plus the SA-4 Pat Hand and Long Track radars. Codes must be unique across all tables.

defaultTables.name: Example - DTC SA-2 codes (User Manual)
defaultTables.description: User Manual example showing SAM system, FCR and EWR codes for the SA-2 entered in TBL1.

tips: Use POS only against known, fixed sites (or mobile SAMs confirmed stationary via TGP/HMCS markpoint); mobile battalions (e.g. SA-4) are better attacked with HAD or HAS. (Training Manual 12)
In POS the WPN page cannot tell you whether the radar is emitting; use the RWR and a quick Cursor Enable toggle to HAS to check. (Training Manual 12)
Prefer handing off the SAM system (e.g. "2") instead of a single radar (e.g. "2T"), especially for SEAD. (Training Manual 12)

HARM range in BMS is up to ~60 NM (motor burn ~45 s, Mach 3+), longer than any Korean SAM ring (SA-10 50 NM, SA-5 53 NM). Valid shots are possible beyond 60 NM but a missile fired too early self-destructs when its battery runs out - wait for the in-range cues. Azimuth off the nose reduces range. (Training Manual 12)

SEAD: time TOT/TUI so impacts cover the package trespass (e.g. 4 HARMs, one impact every 15 s for a 1-minute trespass = PET shots). DEAD: fire just outside the ring (21-20 NM for the SA-2), continue inbound until the FCR appears on the RWR, then put the emitter on the beam and watch for launches. (Training Manual 12)

Missiles keep their own handed-off threat, submode and mode per station (MSL STEP), but the steerpoint is always the current one - change steerpoint before the second shot at a different location. (Dash-34 4.2.5.1.5.3, Training Manual 12)
Keep the FCR in CRM/an A-A mode during HARM work for air SA; switch to MRM override if threatened. (Dash-34 4.2.5.1.3, Training Manual 12)

The fire control radar is the priority target: destroying only the search radar does not stop the SAM, but forces its FCR to radiate longer, which improves the next HARM shot. With enough missiles, target both. (Training Manual 12, Threat Guide)
HTS triangulation needs bearing change: beam the emitter to go from PGM5 to PGM1 - a PGM5 shot can miss by several miles. (Dash-34 4.2.5.1.8.2, Training Manual 12)
With HAS, limit the active table with the SRCH page when more than 10 emitters could be present, otherwise relevant threats may not be displayed. (Training Manual 12)
After a HARM leaves, expect an asymmetric store condition - trim. (Training Manual 12)
A destroyed PPT threat ring can be removed from the HSD with TMS down on its PPT. (Training Manual 12)

HAD location of any emitter can be turned into a markpoint (FPM on the TD box, HUD mark mode) for TGP identification - at least one HARM must be loaded for the TD box to appear. (Training Manual 28.5)

SAMs got smarter since 4.35: radars shut down, SA and FC radars are separate entities, and some SAMs can shoot down incoming missiles. HARMs miss when the target radar goes silent - use TI/GS options and bait tactics. (Training Manual 12.3)
Optimal SEAD/DEAD altitude blocks: above 30,000 ft AGL or 50-300 ft AGL; keep 350 kts or more. (Training Manual 28.4)
gaps: No HTS/HAD threat class tables exist in the BMS 4.38 docs (the HTS detects all emitters; htsClasses left empty).
No default/suggested ALIC table set-ups per theater in the docs (DTC defaults are 0000); only the training examples are given.
Dash-34 ALIC table has no SHIP entries; several radars have no ALIC code (Spoon Rest-only systems, IR SAMs).
FCR names for the SA-8 (608), Nike (696) and Skyguard (695) rows are blank in the Dash-34 table.
alicCodeNotes: Threat Guide chart differences vs Dash-34: SA-6 EWR listed as Flat Face 403 "F"; SA-15 HARM symbol "15T" (Dash-34: "15"); SA-19 "19T" (Dash-34: "19"); SA-5 also has Odd Group (HARM "5A", no ALIC code). (BMS Threat Guide p.41)
Codes can be entered as 3 or 4 digits (e.g. 102 or 0102). IDs must be unique across TBL1-TBL3. (User Manual 5.1.7, Dash-34 4.2.5.1.1)
